smell a rat: When the stranger offered me a free phone in return for my bank password, I began to smell a rat.
當那個陌生人說要用我的銀行密碼換一支免費手機時，我開始覺得可疑。
smell trouble: As soon as the two angry fans started shouting at each other, the guard could smell trouble coming.
那兩名憤怒的球迷一開始互相大吼，警衛就嗅到麻煩要來了。
smell of success: After three straight wins, the whole team was filled with confidence and the sweet smell of success.
連贏三場之後，全隊充滿了信心和甜美的成功的味道。
smell fishy: His story about losing his homework on the bus three times this week really smells fishy to the teacher.
他這星期第三次說作業掉在公車上，老師覺得這說法真的很可疑。
come up smelling of roses: Even though the plan failed badly, the clever manager somehow came up smelling of roses and kept his job.
雖然計畫徹底失敗，那位精明的經理卻不知怎麼地安然無恙，保住了工作。
smooth the way: The new trade agreement will smooth the way for local farmers to sell their fruit in Japan.
新的貿易協定將為本地農民在日本銷售水果鋪平道路。
smooth over differences: The two leaders met for dinner to smooth over differences that had grown between their countries.
兩位領袖共進晚餐，以緩和兩國之間日漸擴大的分歧。
smooth out problems: Before the school trip, the teachers held a meeting to smooth out problems with the bus schedule.
校外教學之前，老師們開會消除遊覽車時刻表的問題。
smooth one's hair: Before the job interview, she looked in the mirror and quickly smoothed her hair with her hand.
面試之前，她照了照鏡子，很快地用手撫平頭髮。
smooth the transition: The school offers a summer camp to smooth the transition for new students so they feel less nervous.
學校舉辦夏令營，讓新生的過渡順利，使他們不那麼緊張。
snap at someone: Please don't snap at me in such an angry voice; I was only trying to help you with your homework.
請不要用那麼生氣的語氣對我厲聲說話；我只是想幫你寫作業而已。
snap up a bargain: Shoppers lined up outside the store at dawn, hoping to snap up a bargain on the first day of the sale.
購物者天一亮就在店外排隊，希望在特賣第一天搶購便宜貨。
snap out of it: You've been sad about the game for a week; it's time to snap out of it and start practicing again.
你為了那場比賽難過一個星期了；該振作起來，重新開始練習了。
snap under pressure: Some players play well in practice but snap under pressure when thousands of fans are watching them.
有些球員練習時表現很好，但在數千名球迷注視下卻在壓力下崩潰。
snap a photo: When we saw the beautiful sunset over the sea, my sister quickly took out her phone to snap a photo.
當我們看到海上美麗的夕陽時，我姊姊很快拿出手機拍照。
snap one's fingers: When the magician snaps his fingers, the coin in his hand suddenly disappears in front of the children.
當魔術師彈手指時，他手中的硬幣就在孩子們面前突然消失。
a snap decision: Don't make a snap decision about which university to choose; take some time to think it over.
選哪一所大學不要做倉促決定；花點時間好好考慮。
snatch victory: With only two seconds left, our team scored a goal to snatch victory from the stronger team.
只剩兩秒時，我們的隊伍踢進一球，從較強的隊伍手中奪得勝利。
snatch a bag: A thief on a motorcycle tried to snatch a bag from an old woman walking down the street.
一名騎機車的小偷試圖從一位走在街上的老婦人手中搶包包。
snatch some sleep: During the long flight, I tried to snatch some sleep between meals, but the baby next to me kept crying.
在漫長的飛行中，我試著在兩餐之間抓緊時間睡一下，但旁邊的嬰兒一直哭。
snatch a glimpse: Fans waited outside the hotel for hours, hoping to snatch a glimpse of the famous singer as she hurried by.
粉絲們在飯店外等了好幾個小時，希望能在那位知名歌手匆匆走過時匆匆一瞥。
snatch defeat from the jaws of victory: We were leading by ten points, but we made silly mistakes and managed to snatch defeat from the jaws of victory.
我們原本領先十分，卻犯了愚蠢的錯誤，結果煮熟的鴨子飛了。
sneak out of the house: The boy tried to sneak out of the house quietly at midnight without waking his parents, but the dog barked.
男孩半夜想在不吵醒父母的情況下悄悄溜出家門，但狗叫了起來。
sneak a look: While the teacher wasn't watching, Tom tried to sneak a look at his classmate's test paper.
趁老師沒注意時，湯姆想偷看同學的考卷。
sneak up on: My little brother likes to sneak up on me quietly and shout "Boo!" to scare me.
我弟弟喜歡悄悄接近我，然後大喊「哇！」來嚇我。
sneak into the cinema: Without buying tickets, the two teenagers tried to sneak into the cinema through the back door.
那兩個青少年沒買票，想從後門偷溜進電影院。
sneak preview: The film company offered fans a sneak preview of the new movie a week before it opened in theaters.
電影公司在新片上映前一週讓影迷搶先看。
sniff out the truth: The reporter spent months asking questions, determined to sniff out the truth about the missing money.
那名記者花了好幾個月追問，決心查出失蹤款項的真相。
sniff at the offer: The famous chef sniffed at the offer of a small salary, saying it was far too low for someone like him.
那位名廚對微薄薪水的提議嗤之以鼻，說這對像他這樣的人來說太低了。
not to be sniffed at: A prize of ten thousand dollars is not to be sniffed at, so I'm going to enter the contest.
一萬元的獎金不可小覷，所以我要報名參加比賽。
sniff out a bargain: My mother can always sniff out a bargain at the night market, and she never pays full price.
我媽媽總能在夜市找到便宜貨，而且她從不付全額。
sniff the air: Dogs often stop to sniff the air when they walk past a restaurant full of delicious smells.
狗經過充滿美味香氣的餐廳時，常常會停下來嗅空氣。
